texts.preamble: Kishore Kumar Talwani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 March, 2022 Author: Atul Sreedharan Bench: Atul Sreedharan 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Atul Sreedha On The 25th Of March, 2 Misc. Criminal Case No. 16115 of 20 Between:- Kishore Kumar Talwani S/O Late Shri Sudama Lal Talwani, Aged About 51 Years, Occupation: Proprietor Sudama Store (Flour Mill) 19, Kali Parade Industrial Area, Near Chhola Road, By-Pass, Bhopal R/O A-1, B.N.B. Colony, Idgah Hills, Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) (By Shri Shobhitaditya, Advocate ) And The State Of Madhya Pradesh Through Shri Bhojaraj Singh Dhakad Food Inspector Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) (By Shri Piyush Bhatnagar, Panel Lawyer) This petition coming on for admission this da following: Order
texts.facts: The present petition has been filed by the petitioner herein for the quash of proceedings pending against him being RCT No.1375 of 2011 in the Court of the learned XIth Civil Judge, Class-I and Special Magistrate (Prevention of Food Adulteration Act) Bhopal. 2. Brief facts in this case are as follows:- A shop of the petitioner, who was the owner and proprietor of Sudama Store (Flour Kishore Kumar Talwani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86741941/ 1 Mill) was inspected by the respondent on 22.05.2010 and the sample of Besan and red chilli powder were taken. The report of the Public Analyst was submitted on 28.06.2010 in which the red chilli powder was alleged to have been adulterated. Sanction was granted on 16.12.2010 for the prosecution of the petitioner herein. On 17.02.2011, the respondent filed the charge-sheet against the SAN petitioner and summons were issued to him. Upon the petitioner's appearing on 30.01.2012, he applied for reanalysis of the sample of red chilli powder. The learned trial Court allowed the application for reanalysis vide order dated 26.03.2012 and requisite charges were submitted by the applicant/petitioner through demand draft on 11.04.2012 for an amount of Rs.1,000/-. Vide order dated 13.04.2012, the learned trial Court directed the Deputy Director, Food and Drug Administration to produce the second part of the sample for its analysis at the Central Food Laboratory. The second part of the sample was not produced in spite of several reminders and finally the second part of the sample of the alleged adulterated red chilli powder was produced before the trial Court on 05.12.2018, after 18 months since the collection of the said sample. The provisions under Section 13(2)(a) of the Food Adulteration Act specify that such sample should be produced within a period of 5 days from the requisition by the trial Court. The second part of the sample was sent for analysis to the Central Food Laboratory on 05.12.2012 and the report came from the Central Food Laboratory on 01.06.2016, i.e. after 4 years from the dispatch of the sample and 6 years from the date of its collection. The report reveals that it was unfit for analysis. 3. The brief facts reveal that the petitioner does not have the benefit of a report from the Central Food Laboratory at Ghaziabad as the respondent has delayed in producing the second part of the sample of red chilli powder before the trial Court and thereafter it languished to the Central Food Laboratory for almost four years after which the report was received by the learned trial Court to the effect that it was found unfit for analysis.
